lecture_beats.subject: Angular conservation and effective radial motion
Experimental origin, outlook, and explicit time dependence

resolved_source_issues.issue: ASR briefly makes U(r) sound equal to theta.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter follows the surrounding argument: a central potential depends on r and not theta.

resolved_source_issues.issue: ASR blurs derivatives with respect to q and q-dot.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Canonical momentum and the Euler-Lagrange equation are restored from the completed board and context.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The spoken rotation signs wobble while the example is developed.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The settled convention delta x=-epsilon y and delta y=epsilon x is used consistently.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The cube discussion is heavily garbled.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Only the stable distinction between discrete and continuous symmetry is retained.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The sign of the time-induced displacement is repeatedly reconsidered.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The fixed-time sampling argument gives delta q=-epsilon q-dot and preserves the reversed-slope check.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Endpoint labels and overhang names change during the spoken derivation.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Fixed t1 and t2 notation preserves the argument without the label drift.
The standard regularity condition is stated as a clearly identified mathematical refinement.
